gaps.explanation: No business-type detail lines. Proprietary funds statement of revenues, expenses and changes in fund net position (p9 Water/Sewer/Electric columns, p10 Storm Water/Solid Waste/Total Enterprise/Internal Service, printed pp26-27). JSON business-type receipts = Total Enterprise operating revenues 20,529,683 + Gain (loss) on disposal of asset 130 + Investment earnings 1,655,403 = 22,185,216. Added one line per non-zero enterprise cell (Internal Service Fund excluded). Row checks: Charges for services 4,249,444 + 7,882,084 + 2,659,412 = 14,790,940; Franchise fees Electric 4,404,119; Fees, taxes, permits and licenses 82,051 + 62,490 + 367,168 + 1,100 = 512,809; Sales tax 33,719 + 482,860 + 25,095 = 541,674; Misc operating revenues 229,782 + 31,567 + 18,792 = 280,141; Gain on disposal Water 130; Investment earnings 551,996 + 803,563 + 92,239 + 54,268 + 153,337 = 1,655,403. Column operating totals as printed: Water 4,594,996, Sewer 8,459,001, Electric 4,404,119, Storm Water 392,263, Solid Waste 2,679,304. Sum of added lines 22,185,216 = statement.

gaps.explanation: Statement (p6, 1/2 Cent Sales Tax Fund column) prints 'Proceeds from bond issuance' 5,055,000 (= debt_proceeds) and 'Original issue premium' 77,483 (= other_financing 77,483) on separate rows. The 1/2 Sales Tax budget-basis schedule (p16) prints one line 'Proceeds from long-term debt, net' 5,132,483 (detail, other financing) = 5,055,000 + 77,483. The money is in detail once; the 77,483 gap is the premium, which the statement side keeps in other_financing while the schedule includes it in its single proceeds line. Replacing the schedule line would mean swapping a printed schedule line for statement cells; no line is missing, so no fix.
